On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for accused has argued that accused has been falsely implicated in the present case and that there is contradiction in the testimony of prosecution witnesses.

Now moving to case in hand, we find that PW4 i.e. KS Kusma who was deputed as Identification Officer in the said examination found during checking that accused Vikrant was appearing in the name of Abhishek Kesari and she has correctly identified the accused in court. PW5 and PW6 has also correctly identified the accused Vikrant Kumar in court.

13 . Further perusal of evidence of PW1, PW2 and PW3 shows that they could not identify the accused as their evidences were being recorded after the 10 years and they have deposed that the matter is very old.

But they have narrated all the incident in line with the prosecution story and stated that accused Vikrant Kumar was appearing on behalf / name of Abishek Keshari on the roll no. 3510 in room no. 201.
This fact is corroborating with the testimony given by PW4.

The fact that the 3 witnesses have not identified the accused in court does not affect the prosecution case as out of 4 public witnesses one witness who was specifically deputed as identification officer has identified him and all the other witness has not deposed that he is not the same person rather they deposed that they cannot identify the accused at the matter is very old.
Hence it is not case of wrong identification of accused.
14. In general, persons appearance get changed in 10 years and that is the case here and accused cannot be benefited for this.
FIR No. 195 /2010, PS Jamia Nagar State vs. Vikrant Kumar PAGE 15 OF PAGE 20

entities.text: PS Jamia Nagar State vs. Vikrant Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover memory also goes faded in 10 years still not a PW has deposed that accused is not the same person.
Though earlier opportunity to identify tends to minimize the chances of the memory of the witness fading away due to long lapse of time.
But delay in identification cannot be a ground to total acquittal when other evidences are available.

15. In addition to, PW2, who was on invigilation duty in the given room has deposed that when he was verifying the candidate he found that the person who is sitting on the seat allotted was different from the person whose picture appeared in the ID/ admit card.

The same is deposed by the other witnesses i.e. PW3 has also said that as a part of his duty he was checking and verifying candidate physically and he was on invigilator duty in room no.201 on 30.05.2010 and he handed over one student to authority.
This statement of PW3 is also corroborating with the fact that PW1, PW2 and PW4 has already deposed that some person has impersonated as Abhishek Kesari on 30.05.2010 in room no. 201.

Also PW1, PW2, PW3, PW4 have deposed that timing of examination was 10 am to 1 pm and accused was apprehended at around 11.30 am and it is not the case here that room no. 201 many persons were apprehended impersonating except the accused.
Hence his presence is also proved at crime spot/ inside the room.
16. Moreover accused could not justify his presence inside the FIR No. 195 /2010, PS Jamia Nagar State vs. Vikrant Kumar PAGE 16 OF PAGE 20 room no. 201 and at the fixed seat of Abhishek Kesari.

Moreover all the public witnesses have admitted that offence has been committed in FIR No. 195 /2010, PS Jamia Nagar State vs. Vikrant Kumar PAGE 17 OF PAGE 20 room no. 201 roll no. 3510 which is matching with the Ex.P1 i.e. photograph of the roll number along with the accused.

With respect to argument that some witnesses have not identified the accused in court, the undersigned does not find himself in agreement with this as they were not hostile in toto and whatever they have stated is corroborating with each other and this is all because of long time lapsed from the date of the commission of the crime and in the date of deposition.

Hon'ble supreme court has reiterated in Paulmeli v. State of Tamil Nadu: (2014) 13 SCC 90 that even the testimony of a hostile witness cannot be rejected in toto as the evidentiary value of his testimony is not lost and can be accepted to the extent that the version is found corroborated with other material evidence.

20. 21.

Now coming to the section 416 IPC the ingredients are 1. if he cheats by pretending to be some other person,
2. or by knowingly substituting one person for another,
3. or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is.

8 22.

Here from the facts and from the perusal of the admit card (Ex.P1 and Mark X) it is clear that admit card for roll no. 3510 was issued for one Abhishek Kesari and not for accused Vikrant and accused has falsely marked attendance as Abhishek Kesari on the attendance sheet (Mark Z) and accused was found sitting on the seat of Abhishek Kesari and was giving the examination it is also cleared that he was pretending to be some other person i.e. Abhishek Kesari and knew that he was committing the impersonation of being Abhishek Kesari for the examination and his this act is likely to cause damage / harm to JMI University reputation and to other genuine candidate's future and seat /admission in JMI University.
Additionally the accused did not reveal his genuine identity when apprehended and shown himself as Abhishek Kesari.
In cheating by impersonating a person not only cheat but also does so by pretending to be some other person.

Here accused Vikrant Kumar not only cheated the JMI Authorities by representing that he is the Abhishek Kesari but also dishonestly FIR No. 195 /2010, PS Jamia Nagar State vs. Vikrant Kumar PAGE 19 OF PAGE 20 induced them to make him enter and sit in exam.
FSL result also indicate the same.
No material discrepancy is brought to the notice of the court by the accused.
23. From the testimony of PWs, it is proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused Vikrant Kumar has committed the crime of cheating by impersonation and is convicted u/s 419 IPC.
Copy of judgment be given free of cost to convict.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No defence was led by the accused despite opportunity.
This fact is corroborating with the testimony given by PW4.
The fact that the 3 witnesses have not identified the accused in court does not affect the prosecution case as out of 4 public witnesses one witness who was specifically deputed as identification officer has identified him and all the other witness has not deposed that he is not the same person rather they deposed that they cannot identify the accused at the matter is very old.
Hence it is not case of wrong identification of accused.
14. In general, persons appearance get changed in 10 years and that is the case here and accused cannot be benefited for this.
FIR No. 195 /2010, PS Jamia Nagar State vs. Vikrant Kumar PAGE 15 OF PAGE 20
Moreover memory also goes faded in 10 years still not a PW has deposed that accused is not the same person.
Though earlier opportunity to identify tends to minimize the chances of the memory of the witness fading away due to long lapse of time.
But delay in identification cannot be a ground to total acquittal when other evidences are available.
15. In addition to, PW2, who was on invigilation duty in the given room has deposed that when he was verifying the candidate he found that the person who is sitting on the seat allotted was different from the person whose picture appeared in the ID/ admit card.
Accused could not contradict PWs to the aspect that he was not present inside the room or accused did not raise any plea of alibi to show that on the given date and time accused was present at some other place or along with some other persons.
He could not show that he was present inside the room because he was giving his own examination or he could not prove that he was bonafidely sitting at wrong seat.
17. With respect to defence that no expert help was taken to find out whether there was difference in photographs of hall permit and ID card, the undersigned does not find itself in agreement with this as during the examination the invigilator check the ID cards etc and bear visual perusal of the same is sufficient to tell the difference and moreover identification officer has himself has identified the accused as the person who has committed the offence and was appearing on behalf of other.
Hon'ble supreme court has reiterated in Paulmeli v. State of Tamil Nadu: (2014) 13 SCC 90 that even the testimony of a hostile witness cannot be rejected in toto as the evidentiary value of his testimony is not lost and can be accepted to the extent that the version is found corroborated with other material evidence.
The complaint given by PW1 i.e. Ex.PW1/A is not rebutted during the cross examination and accused could not show that the complaint is false and the witnesses of the complaint are already examined in court and they could not be impeached.
20. Accused did not challenge the apology letter Mark X written by him and did not apprise the court in which circumstances it was written by him and in absence of the reason given by the accused, the reason stated in apology letter is also indicating to the fact that FIR No. 195 /2010, PS Jamia Nagar State vs. Vikrant Kumar PAGE 18 OF PAGE 20 accused has done something wrong and that wrong is offence itself.
21.

2. or by knowingly substituting one person for another,
3. or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is.

Additionally the accused did not reveal his genuine identity when apprehended and shown himself as Abhishek Kesari.
